surfaces.dashboard_widget: Always-on 'Send feedback' widget in the dashboard sidebar. Self-selected.
surfaces.cli_post_install: One-line prompt after `e2b template build` completes. Skippable.

notes: Free-text is verbatim. Ratings are 1-5 where collected; the widget does not ask for one.
product_area is picked by the respondent from a fixed list, not assigned by us.
Org role (admin/member/billing) is not captured on any surface.
Respondents who never completed signup are not reachable by any of these surfaces.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Took me a while to work out that my API key belongs to a workspace and not to me. I generated one from my personal workspace, wired it into our staging service, then nobody else on the team could see the sandboxes it spawned. Not obvious anywhere in the UI which workspace you are currently in.

Template builds are slow and silent. Six minutes staring at a spinner with no layer output. I genuinely could not tell whether it was building or wedged, so I killed it twice before letting one finish.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Honestly nothing. Key, npm install, sandbox running inside ten minutes. The quickstart is the shortest of any infra product we evaluated this quarter.

I wanted to add two engineers to our workspace and hit a wall I did not understand. The invite button is there, it just does nothing useful until billing is set up, and the message does not say that. Spent twenty minutes assuming it was a bug.

responses.prompt: How did that build go?
responses.text: Second build of an unchanged Dockerfile took almost as long as the first. If there is a layer cache I cannot tell when it hits, and nothing in the output says either way.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Getting a sandbox up was easy. Understanding pause and resume was not. I could not find a clear statement of what survives a pause, so I assumed nothing did and rebuilt state on every run for a week.

Our security review stalled on one question I could not answer from the docs or the dashboard: can a workspace member revoke or read a key created by another member? We need a permissions matrix on a page somewhere, not a support thread.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Startup is fast, which is the whole reason we picked this. What I could not predict was the variance. Most starts are well under a second, then one in twenty takes four or five, and our agent loop has no idea whether to retry.

I burned through my credits overnight because a test suite left sandboxes running. No warning email, no soft cap, just a stopped account in the morning. A usage alert at 80% would have saved the whole incident.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: The mental model of personal workspace versus team workspace never landed for me. I think I now have sandboxes split across two workspaces and no way to move them. Would like a single 'switch workspace' control that is visible on every page.

responses.prompt: How did that build go?
responses.text: Once I moved our heavy apt install into the template instead of doing it at runtime, cold starts dropped from thirty seconds to under one. Enormous difference. This should be the loudest advice in the templates docs.

Invited a colleague, they accepted, and they still could not see our templates. Turned out the invite put them somewhere different from where the templates live. Two hours of confusion that a clearer workspace name in the invite email would have prevented.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: I could not tell which key was safe to paste into a shared repo secret and which was tied to just me. Ended up creating four keys and deleting three. The key list needs to say what each key can reach.

Had about ninety minutes this morning where sandbox creation kept failing in Frankfurt while everything was green on the status page. Retrying against the US region worked. Being told 'degraded, use another region' in the dashboard would have beaten discovering it ourselves.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: The async API is clean and the types are right, which is rarer than it should be. I had a working code interpreter loop before lunch.
Build logs disappear the moment the build finishes, so a failed build is only debuggable if you happened to be watching. Please keep the last few builds' logs around in the dashboard.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Docs are good for the happy path and thin after it. I wanted one page on running this in production: timeouts, retries, what to do when a sandbox dies mid-run. Ended up reconstructing it from blog posts.
Tried to hand our workspace over to a teammate while I am on leave and there is apparently no way to transfer ownership from the UI. That is a strange gap for a product sold to teams.

responses.prompt: How did that build go?
responses.text: Build worked but I had no idea it would take eight minutes. A rough estimate up front, or even just a layer counter, would make the wait feel less broken.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Pricing per sandbox-second is fair and easy to reason about. What I could not find was what an idle paused sandbox costs, and I still am not certain.

Second person from our team writing in about this. We now have three workspaces because each of us made one on signup, and consolidating means recreating every template by hand. An import or merge path would help a lot.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Signed up, got a key, ran a sandbox, then stopped when I tried to bring the rest of the team in. The invite screen asks for a role and I have no idea what the roles actually allow. Parked it until someone can explain.
Would like a way to see all running sandboxes across the whole workspace with who started them. Right now a runaway job is invisible until the bill moves.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Nothing hard. We had our evaluation harness running against real sandboxes on day one, and the isolation story answered most of what our security team asked.

The permissions change that landed this week made things worse for us, not better. Keys my teammates created stopped working in CI until each of them re-issued one, and nothing told us that would happen.

responses.prompt: How did that build go?
responses.text: Fine once I learned to keep the template small. Would still like a warning when a template crosses some size where starts get slow, because I found that boundary by accident.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: I run a four person team and I could not answer 'who can spend money here' after ten minutes of clicking. That is the question my finance lead asks before I can roll this out.
The pause and resume docs improved, thank you. Still missing the limits: how long can something stay paused, and what happens to it after that. We are designing around a guess.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Smooth start. One snag: the code interpreter examples assume a notebook style and I was calling from a FastAPI worker, so I had to work out the lifecycle myself.

Following up on my earlier note. We got there in the end, but only after a support thread explained that keys are workspace scoped and cannot be moved. Please put that sentence in the key creation dialog.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Second attempt at rolling this out to my team. The invite flow asked me to add a payment method before I could add anyone, which I was not expecting on a trial, so I stopped again.
Uptime has been fine for us, no complaints there. The thing that bites is silent timeouts on long running sandboxes, where the process just stops and the error does not say why.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Getting our internal base image into a template took a day, mostly because I could not tell which parts of a Dockerfile you support. A supported and unsupported list would have saved most of that.
Still waiting on the permissions matrix I asked about three weeks ago. Our procurement checklist has a literal box for it. This is now the only thing between us and signing.

responses.prompt: How did that build go?
responses.text: Much better than my first attempt a month ago. Builds feel quicker and I can see what is happening now. Upgraded to Pro on the back of it.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Fast and predictable for us. The one gap is observability: I would like to export sandbox lifecycle events to our own stack rather than reading the dashboard.

Now that we are set up, the workspace model is fine. Getting here was the problem. If you fixed one thing, make the first-run screen ask whether this is personal or for a team, and set everything up accordingly.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Came back to add my two colleagues and gave up again. The roles are called owner, admin and developer, and nowhere does it say what a developer cannot do. I am not granting access I do not understand.
Invoice arrived with one line item for the whole workspace. We need per-project or at least per-key attribution, otherwise I cannot charge this back to the teams using it.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Easiest infra onboarding I have done this year. We moved our whole agent test harness over in an afternoon and it has been stable since.
Update from my earlier message: we are live with four people. It took a call with support to understand that keys do not move between workspaces. Everything after that was easy.

responses.prompt: What was the hardest part of getting started?
responses.text: Access is settled now but the July change cost us a day of CI. If you touch key scoping again, mail the workspace owners first.
